findings.reason: Blocks C and E overlap at (5,2), so the proposed five blocks cannot all be torn out intact.

findings.quote: Thus after tearing out these \(5\) blocks in each \(5\times5\) cell there is no triple left anywhere in the \(n\times n\) square.
findings.reason: Even the union of the specified blocks leaves row 1, columns 1–3 untouched in each macrosquare. This is a remaining horizontal triple, contradicting maximality.
For n=1 this gives −2 potential triples, whereas there are zero. The counting formula requires n≥2.

reason: The lower-bound counting argument works for n≥2, but the upper-bound construction both overlaps blocks and leaves an available triple. Consequently the proof does not establish the requested bounds.
